title: Weekly refresh never commits: `git add` aborts on the per-season files its own builders write
failure: First real execution (the Tuesday after week 1). `build_team_week.py --seasons 2026-2026` writes BOTH `cache/team_week_2026_v1.parquet` (per-season, scripts/build_team_week.py:235) and `cache/team_week_2026_2026_v1.parquet` (combined, :242); `build_player_week.py` does the same (:552 and :563). `.gitignore` un-ignores only the `YYYY_YYYY` form (`!cache/player_week_20[2-9][0-9]_20[2-9][0-9]_v1.parquet`), so the single-season files stay ignored. The shell expands `cache/player_week_*_v1.parquet cache/team_week_*_v1.parquet` to literal paths INCLUDING the two ignored ones, and `git add` given an explicitly named ignored path exits 1. Steps run under `bash -e`, so the step dies before `git diff --cached`, `git commit` and `git push`. Net effect: the job fails every week from week 1 onward and the current-season table is NEVER pushed, so the deployed site keeps projecting mid-season as if the season had not started — precisely the silent degradation the workflow header says it exists to prevent. Note the failure only occurs when there IS something to commit: before week 1 the glob matches only the tracked 2016-2025 files, `git add` succeeds and the job reports "no change this week", so it looks healthy right up to the moment it matters.
fix: Name the two files explicitly instead of globbing, e.g. `git add "cache/player_week_${Y}_${Y}_v1.parquet" "cache/team_week_${Y}_${Y}_v1.parquet"` using steps.season.outputs.year, or restrict the glob to the double-year form (`cache/player_week_*_*_v1.parquet`). Adding `-f` would be wrong: it would commit the ignored per-season files too.

title: routes_run_proxy is zero-filled when participation is unpublished, collapsing four trained features to 0 for every in-season projection
failure: `routes_run_proxy` is in VOLUME_STATS (features.py:67), so `add_player_history` builds f_career_/f_r3_/f_r8_/f_std_routes_run_proxy from it, and all four are in the shipped registry's feature list. But the source is participation data, which the repo itself documents as unavailable in season (gridlib/fetch.py:209 "Publishes only AFTER the postseason and does not update in season"; scripts/build_player_week.py:22 "TRAINING-ONLY"). When it is missing, `_routes()` returns an empty frame (build_player_week.py:119-121), the left merge yields an all-NaN column, and `_prior_mean` / `_prior_roll_mean` zero-fill it (features.py:313, 352). So every game in the CURRENT season contributes routes=0 to the player's history. From roughly week 4 of a live season, f_r3/f_r8/f_std_routes_run_proxy read exactly 0.00 for the entire league, where in training a starting WR carries ~32. The frozen 2016-2025 backfill keeps its real values, so this is invisible to every test. Verified 2026-09-06: fetch.load_participation(2026) returns None. Reproducing it by nulling 2025's routes and rebuilding features + predicting with the shipped joblibs over 4,746 week-6+ rows: targets 3.102 -> 2.291 (-26.2%), receptions 2.101 -> 1.519 (-27.7%), carries 6.184 -> 4.880 (-21.1%), attempts 26.774 -> 23.720 (-11.4%), receiving_yards -14.6%. Every projection on the board is understated by a fifth to a quarter for most of the season, and the error grows week by week as the rolling windows fill with zeros.
fix: routes_run_proxy is a count whose SOURCE is structurally absent, not a count that is genuinely zero, so `_prior_mean`'s zero-fill is the wrong discipline for it (it is the same distinction the module already draws for ngs_/pfr_ rates at features.py:397). Either route it through `_prior_mean_skipna` and add a skipna variant of `_prior_roll_mean`, or drop the four routes features from the shipped set and retrain, since `off_snaps` is the live exposure proxy and is unaffected (f_r3_off_snaps was identical in both runs). Whichever is chosen, add a serve-time assertion that no trained feature is >90% NaN-or-constant on the live rows, and extend the weekly workflow's sanity check (.github/workflows/weekly.yml) from "columns present" to "columns populated at the rate the history has".

title: Cold project_week peaks at ~1.4 GB RSS, over the ~1 GB container limit
failure: A visitor opens gridironvalue.streamlit.app for a week whose predictions_{season}_w{NN}_m1.parquet is absent (it is gitignored — `.gitignore` line `cache/predictions_*.parquet` — so a fresh Streamlit Cloud clone has NONE). app.py:185 calls project_week_cached, which falls through to project_week and runs F.build over the 63,042-row x 177-column backfill concatenated with the constructed inference rows. Measured on this machine with the real serving import chain (streamlit + sklearn + plotly + polars + pyarrow loaded first, which alone is 228 MB RSS): project_week ran 22.2 s and hit a peak RSS of 1434 MB, ending resident at 1026 MB. On a ~1 GB container the process is OOM-killed and the page never renders. Even the sub-step is over budget: F.build alone on the backfill peaks at 1044 MB from a 307 MB baseline. Memory is also not returned — after `del out; gc.collect()` RSS stayed at 585-711 MB across repeated runs, so a container that survives one build carries ~350-475 MB of retained arena into the next request.
fix: Two things have to change together. (a) Stop building features over ten years of history inside a web request: precompute and commit the per-week feature rows (or the projections themselves) the way player_week_20NN_20NN_v1.parquet is already committed by .github/workflows/weekly.yml, and have project_week_cached read them. (b) If the in-request build must stay, cut the working set: `del hist` after the concat on line 339, restrict `combined` to the feature columns the registry actually needs plus the group keys, and downcast the 126 float64 columns to float32 (halves the frame).

title: latest_depth_chart reloads and deep-copies the whole 499k-row depth-chart file on each of its 32 calls per week
failure: build_inference_rows loops over the 16 games of a week and, for each of the two teams, calls fetch.latest_depth_chart. That is 32 calls. Every call goes to fetch.py:649 `dc = load_depth_charts(season)`, which is not memoized: it re-reads depth_charts_2026.parquet from disk (498,892 rows x 13 cols, 292 MB deep in memory) and then runs _attach_week_from_timestamp, which does a full `out = df.copy()` (fetch.py:366) of that same 292 MB frame plus a fresh `load_schedules()` (fetch.py:369). All of that work is thrown away to keep 21 rows. Measured: build_inference_rows takes 17.3 s and drives RSS from 147 MB to 476 MB (peak 557 MB) to produce a 609-row frame. Per-call cost measured at 0.47-0.57 s with RSS climbing ~100 MB per call and never coming back (140 -> 331 -> 433 -> 464 MB across three calls with gc.collect() between each). This is roughly 15 of the 22 seconds and several hundred MB of the OOM in the finding above.
fix: Load the season's chart once per week build: hoist `load_depth_charts(season)` out of the loop and pass the frame down, or put `@lru_cache(maxsize=2)` on `load_depth_charts` (and on `load_schedules`). Filter to `week == week` and `pos_abb.isin(SKILL_POSITIONS)` once, then group by team. Also drop the `out = df.copy()` at fetch.py:366 — the function only assigns a new `week` column.

title: "Kicking Points" is priced and graded in the wrong units (FG count + XP attempts, not points)
failure: STAT_MAP["kicking points"] = (("fg_made", "pat_att"), 1.0) with the comment "# approximated below", but nothing below approximates anything: compare() at line 910 does model_val = sum(vals) * scale, so the model value is FG_made + PAT_att (a count, ~3-5) against a line posted in POINTS (7.5-9.5). Every one of the 31 Kicking Points lines on the committed board is frozen leaning Less with a manufactured -4 to -5.6 gap. Worse, grade() re-resolves the same columns at line 1046, so "actual" is computed in the same wrong units. Verified: a kicker who makes 3 FG + 3 XP = 12 real kicking points against an 8.5 line (a clear More) is graded actual=6.0, result="Less", model_correct=True. The record books a loss as a win, 31 times on week 1 alone, and week_scorecard's mae/line_mae are polluted with it.
fix: Either map it as (("fg_made","pat_att"), ...) with per-column weights (3 for fg_made, 1 for pat_made) rather than a single scalar `scale`, or move "kicking points" into REFUSE until a weighted mapping exists. A single float scale cannot express 3*FG + 1*XP.

title: Kicking Points scores a field goal as 1 point instead of 3, and grade() re-uses the same wrong formula as the "actual"
failure: PrizePicks Kicking Points = 3 x FG made + 1 x XP. STAT_MAP maps it to ("fg_made", "pat_att") with scale 1.0, and compare() at props.py:911 does model_val = sum(vals) * scale, i.e. fg_made + pat_att. On the committed frozen week-1 board all 31 Kicking Points rows lean "Less": mean served model 3.99 against lines of 5.5-9.5, while the correctly scored projection averages 7.40. Re-scoring the 30 rows that also have an FG Made row (3*fg + pat) puts 17 of 30 on the WRONG SIDE (e.g. Harrison Butker: served 4.21 vs line 7.5 -> Less; true 3(1.97)+2.24 = 8.15 -> More). The same formula is then used for grading: ACTUAL_MAP (props.py:1002) carries fg_made and pat_att, so grade() computes actual = fg_made + pat_att. A kicker who makes 2 FG and 3 XP scores 9 real kicking points and beats a 7.5 line, but grade() returns actual=5.0, result="Less", and marks the model's always-"Less" lean model_correct=True. Every kicker line is a manufactured hit in the frozen season record.
fix: Score it as 3*fg_made + pat_att (or a pat_made projection) both in compare() and in grade(). A tuple-of-columns sum cannot express a weighted sum, so kicking points needs its own branch like the "__prob__" one, or a per-column weight in STAT_MAP.

title: "Pass+Rush+Rec TDs" builds the Poisson lambda without passing_tds, so every QB row is priced at near 0%
failure: The stat is mapped to ("__prob__", "rushing_tds", "receiving_tds"), which omits passing_tds. compare() (props.py:889-897) sums only cols[1:] into lam, so a QB projected 1.9 passing TDs and 0.22 rushing TDs gets lam = 0.22 instead of 2.12. Against the standard 1.5 line, threshold_for_line -> 2 and poisson_at_least(0.22, 2) = 0.02, so the row reads 2% and leans "Less"; with the correct lam the module's own poisson_at_least(2.12, 2) = 0.63, i.e. "More". Worse, rank_by_reliability (props.py:551-556) ranks probability rows by |model - 0.5|, so these maximally-wrong rows sort to the TOP of the board. On the committed frozen week-1 board all 9 Pass+Rush+Rec TDs rows lean "Less" with models between 0.00 and 0.14 (Jordan Love 0.00, Josh Allen 0.14) - a stat where the market's 1.5 line implies roughly a coin flip.
fix: Add passing_tds to the tuple for "pass+rush+rec tds" (and to the reliability lookup at props.py:925). Keep "player touchdowns"/"anytime td" as rush+rec only.

title: "Kicking points" is priced as fg_made + pat_att with no scoring weights; every one of the 31 live rows leans the wrong way
failure: A kicker with a posted "Kicking Points" line is scored as fg_made + pat_att (1 point per field goal) instead of 3*fg_made + pat_made. On the saved 2026 week 1 board all 31 kicking-points rows render a model value of 3.28 to 5.02 against lines of 5.5 to 9.5 and therefore ALL lean Less. Applying the real scoring gives 6.20 to 8.88 and flips 18 of the 31 leans to More. The trailing comment promises an approximation that does not exist anywhere in the file.
fix: Map kicking points to a weighted composite (3 x fg_made + pat_made) rather than an unweighted sum, or add it to REFUSE until a weighted path exists. `pat_made` is already in columns.TARGETS but is not a trained target, so either train it or use pat_att as the PAT proxy with the 3x weight on fg_made applied explicitly.

title: grade() silently drops every touchdown and Fantasy Score prop; 44% of the real frozen record is ungradeable and nothing tests it
failure: compare() prices touchdown props through the sentinel tuple ("__prob__", "rushing_tds", "receiving_tds") (props.py:136-141) and fantasy props through ("__fantasy__",). grade() resolves the same tuple and then does `vals = [a.get(ACTUAL_MAP.get(c, c)) for c in cols]`. ACTUAL_MAP has no "__prob__" key, so a.get("__prob__") is None, the next line hits `if any(v is None ...): continue  # did not play, or not scored`, and the row is dropped with no counter. Fantasy rows are dropped one line earlier at props.py:1040. Graded on the committed cache/pp_frozen_2026_w01_v1.json with actuals fabricated for every player (so nothing can be dropped for a genuine DNP): 1022 frozen rows in, 571 graded out, 451 lost - 287 Player Touchdowns, 13 Rec TDs, 12 Rush TDs, 9 Pass+Rush+Rec TDs, 130 Fantasy Score. week_scorecard then reports n=571 as if that were the board. The accuracy record therefore excludes the single largest prop category on the board and says nothing about it. No test in tests/test_props.py grades a kind=="probability" or composite row: test_grade_scores_the_models_lean (line 277) and test_a_frozen_table_can_be_graded (line 730) both use Pass Yards only, and the whole TD block (test_td_prop_uses_probability_not_the_mean, line 812) stops at compare().
fix: In grade(), handle the two sentinels explicitly: for ("__prob__", *stats) sum the actual TD columns and compare the count to the line; for ("__fantasy__",) recompose the PP score from actuals. Count anything still unresolvable into a meta bucket so the page can say "451 lines not gradeable". Add tests that grade one probability row (lean More, 1 TD scored -> hit) and one fantasy row.

title: "Kicking Points" model value is a count of kicks compared to a points line, and grading scores it the same wrong way, so every such row is a guaranteed hit in the public accuracy record
failure: STAT_MAP maps "kicking points" to ("fg_made","pat_att") with scale 1.0, and compare() at gridlib/props.py:911 computes model_val = fg_made + pat_att. Kicking points are 3*FG + 1*PAT, so the Model column prints a KICK COUNT next to a POINTS line. On the committed 2026 week-1 board all 31 Kicking Points rows lean Less, 22 of them survive filter_pickable and render in the ledger, e.g. Brandon Aubrey "Model 4.3 / Line 8.5 / Gap -4.2 / Less" when 3*1.74+2.5 = 7.7 sits essentially on the line. grade() (gridlib/props.py:1046) then builds `actual` from the same two columns, so actual is also a kick count. Real 2025 week 5 kickers graded this way: Ka'imi Fairbairn scored 3 FG + 5 PAT = 14 kicking points (clearly OVER an 8.5 line) but is recorded as actual 8, result Less, model_correct True. All 8 kickers tested graded 8/8 = 100% hits. Those rows feed props.season_record() and therefore the headline "Season record, out of sample: N of M (X%)" plus its Wilson interval that app.py renders under the week board. 22 guaranteed hits out of 529 pickable rows moves a true 50% board to 52.1%, on a page whose whole verdict is whether the lower bound clears 50. week_scorecard's "Model MAE" vs "Line MAE" columns are corrupted the same way (model 4.2 vs actual 4.0 gives mae 1.48 against line_mae 4.62).
fix: Either give the entry a real points composition (a scale cannot express 3*fg_made + 1*pat_att, so it needs its own branch in compare() and a matching branch in grade()'s ACTUAL_MAP path), or move "kicking points" into REFUSE until it can be priced. Do not leave the current mapping shipping to the ledger and the record.

title: Kicking Points is priced and graded as a raw count sum, not points: a 2x-too-small projection that leans Less on every kicker and then grades itself correct ~95% of the time
failure: PrizePicks "Kicking Points" = 3 x FG made + 1 x XP made. STAT_MAP maps it to ("fg_made", "pat_att") with scale 1.0, and compare() at props.py:910 does `sum(vals) * scale`, so the displayed model value is a raw count sum, roughly 1/1.9 of the real quantity. On the COMMITTED 2026 week-1 board (cache/pp_frozen_2026_w01_v1.json, 31 Kicking Points rows) mean model = 3.99 against mean line = 7.40, and ALL 31 rows lean Less; 22 are pickable and 21 survive filter_informed, so 21 rows render on the live ledger as e.g. "Brandon Aubrey / Kicking Points / Model 4.26 / Line 8.5 / Gap -4.2 / Lean Less". The same units error is repeated on the grading side: grade() at props.py:1046-1049 builds `actual` with the identical `sum(...) * scale`, so it scores the pick against fg_made+pat_att instead of 3*fg_made+pat_made. Measured on 2023-2025 kicker games (n=1629): fg_made+pat_att exceeds a 7.5 line 1.9% of the time, while true kicking points exceeds it 46.7%. So the projection error and the grading error point the same way and cancel. Over the 21 shown week-1 lines (3 at 5.5, 7 at 6.5, 8 at 7.5, 4 at 8.5) the site will bank ~20.8 of 22 (94.5%) as HITS into the frozen out-of-sample season record, while the actual bets would win ~10.9 of 22 (49.5%). These are exactly the rows that then feed the "an edge, on this evidence" verdict. The bug also corrupts the week table's Model MAE / Line MAE pair: model error ~0.9 against line error ~3.6 per kicking row, flattering the model by ~2.7 per row for free.
fix: Either weight the components (3*fg_made + pat_made, using made rather than attempted PATs) in both compare() and grade(), or move "kicking points" into REFUSE until it can be priced, the way longest-X props are. Do not leave a stat where the projection and the grader share the same units error.

title: Reflected HTML injection: ?away= / ?home= go raw into an unsafe_allow_html block (working open redirect)
failure:
`away = canonical(st.query_params.get("away"))` (Game.py:88) returns any attacker string, only `.strip().upper()`-ed, and is interpolated into the `_bail()` f-string at line 103, which `store.render_notice()` hands to `st.markdown(..., unsafe_allow_html=True)` at Game.py:60. Any URL whose teams do not resolve reaches this path. Verified live against the app on 127.0.0.1:8571: `/Game?season=2026&week=1&away=&home=SEA` navigated the browser off the page; with `CONTENT="99;URL=HTTPS://EXAMPLE.COM/"` the tag landed verbatim in document.head. Since URL scheme and host are case-insensitive, `CONTENT="0;URL=HTTPS://EVIL.COM/"` is a working open redirect from gridironvalue.streamlit.app to any site - a ready-made phishing link. title: The season record calls anything above 50% "an edge, on this evidence", when the site's own out-of-sample measurement puts the do-nothing bar at 57-60%
failure: season_record() sets beats_coin from `lo > 0.5` (props.py:1121) and props_ui prints "A coin is 50%, so this is an edge, on this evidence." But the null for prop side-picking is not a coin: the site's own validation (docs/lean_probability.csv, produced by scripts/validate_lean_probability.py) measures "always take the more common side" at 56.9% to 60.4% on every prop it grades, and data/stat_reliability.csv line 2 states the bar in words ("picks the right side 67.9% against a 57.0% coin bar"). Concrete failure: 250 graded out-of-sample lines, 145 hits = 58.0%, Wilson 95% CI [51.8, 64.0]. Lower bound clears 50, so the page renders "145 of 250 (58.0%), 95% confidence interval 51.8% to 64.0%. A coin is 50%, so this is an edge, on this evidence." That 58% is inside the range the trivial always-more-common-side rule already achieves, and is BELOW it for receiving yards (59.7%) and rushing yards (60.4%). The site declares an edge on evidence that shows none, on the one page next to real betting decisions, and does so while the footer (gridlib/theme.py:852) claims it "offers no betting advice".
fix: Compare the record against the same benchmark the validation uses (the realised more-common-side rate on the graded rows), not 50%, and only call it an edge when the interval clears that. Failing that, drop the word "edge" and report the rate and interval alone.

title: Depth-chart join uses raw team codes, so OAK/SD never match LV/LAC: 977 player-games lose depth_rank and are labelled non-starters
failure: gridlib/teams.canonical() (OAK->LV, SD->LAC) exists and is unit-tested, but neither depth_chart_normalized() nor this merge calls it. depth_charts_2016.parquet spells the Raiders OAK and the Chargers SD; stats_player_week_2016.parquet spells them LV and LAC. The left merge on [season, week, team, gsis_id] therefore matches nothing for those franchises. Verified: 977 player-week rows (2016 LAC + 2016-2019 LV) have depth_rank null at a rate of exactly 1.000 while every other team runs 0.90-0.98. depth_rank_capped becomes NaN and is_starter, computed as (depth_rank_capped == 1).astype(float), becomes 0.0 because NaN == 1 is False. 79 of those rows are QB games with 20+ pass attempts -- Philip Rivers 2016 wk1 (36 att) and Derek Carr 2016 wk1 (38 att) both train as is_starter = 0.0. depth_rank_capped and is_starter are both in models/registry_m1.json feature_columns, so the models learn from starters mislabelled as backups.
fix: Fold both sides through gridlib.teams.canonical: in depth_chart_normalized (gridlib/fetch.py ~line 739) add out["team"] = out["team"].map(canonical), and canonicalise df["team"] before the merge in build_player_week. Then add a hard check in validate_backfill.py that no team-season has 0% depth_rank coverage.

title: is_home derived by comparing the box-score team code to the schedule's home_team, so 477 HOME player-games get the away side's market and rest features
failure: games.parquet spells the Raiders OAK (2016-2019) and the Chargers SD (2016), while stats_player_week spells them LV and LAC. `is_home = df["team"] == df["home_team"]` is therefore False for every Raiders/Chargers row in those seasons, including their home games. For 477 player-games that ARE home games: team_implied_total and opp_implied_total are swapped, team_spread carries the OPPOSITE SIGN, and rest_days/opp_rest_days are swapped. All four are in models/registry_m1.json feature_columns. Worse, the same row carries is_home = 1 from the team_week merge (which is derived from pbp and is correct), so the row is internally contradictory: the model sees a home game whose spread says the team is a 3-point underdog when the market had it a 3-point favourite. Signed error on team_spread across those rows ranges from -28 to +28.
fix: Do not recompute the home flag from a string compare. The correct flag already arrived from team_week two merges earlier (build_player_week.py:402). Use `is_home = df["is_home"] == 1`, or canonicalise both sides via gridlib.teams.canonical before comparing. Add a hard check to validate_backfill.py asserting (pw.team == pw.home_team) equals pw.is_home for every row.

title: The point-in-time leakage tests exercise a helper defined in the test file, not the feature builder; a real rolling-window leak passes all 259 tests
failure: _prior_games() is defined at tests/test_leakage.py:122 and, by grep across gridlib/, scripts/, app.py, props_ui.py and pages/, is referenced only by three tests in the same file (lines 137, 144, 154). The production point-in-time builders are gridlib/features.py _prior_mean (297), _prior_mean_skipna (319), _prior_sum_and_n (339) and _prior_roll_mean (346). The three tests named as "the canonical leak" (test_history_excludes_the_target_game:133, test_history_is_strictly_before_not_up_to:141, test_a_players_first_ever_game_has_empty_history:151) assert that a filter written three lines above them filters, so they hold by construction and cannot fail for any change to features.py. Concretely: deleting `.shift(1)` from _prior_roll_mean makes every f_r3_*/f_r6_* rolling feature include the current game's own outcome - the exact leak the suite exists to catch, on the largest single block of features - and the suite stays fully green.
fix: Replace the three _prior_games tests with tests that call features.add_player_history on a small synthetic frame and assert f_r3_<col> for row i equals the mean of rows i-3..i-1 only, and that a player's debut row is NaN. Keep _prior_games only if it is used as an independent oracle against the production output.

title: f_team_proe_centered is NaN for 100% of live rows because the league table is pinned to league_season_2016_2025_v1.parquet
failure: `add_team_history` centres PROE with `prior_lg = lg.shift(1)` then `tg["season"].map(prior_lg)`. `lg` comes from gridlib/predict.py:74, hardcoded to `league_season_2016_2025_v1.parquet`, whose index is 2016..2025. A live 2026 row maps to a season absent from the index, so `map` returns NaN and `f_team_proe_centered` is NaN for every projected row, for every week of the season. It is column 108 of the 124 the models were trained on. Nothing catches it: `project_week`'s completeness check (predict.py:350) tests column PRESENCE only, and the column exists. The weekly workflow cannot fix it either — it runs build_team_week.py with `--seasons 2026-2026`, which writes `league_season_2026_2026_v1.parquet` under a different name and does not even commit it (the git add pattern is only player_week_*/team_week_*). In training, only 2016 rows had NaN here (9.6%), so the model's NaN branch for this feature was fitted on 2016 alone, and every 2026 projection is now routed down it. Measured on 2025 rows with the shipped artifacts, blanking the column moves individual projections by up to 3.23 attempts, 12.85 passing yards, 2.21 carries and 6.40 receiving yards.
fix: Make the league table cover the serving season: either version the filename by content and have the weekly job rebuild + commit it (build_team_week.py:247 derives the name from --seasons, so `--seasons 2016-<current>` writes a new name predict.py must then read), or compute the prior-season league PROE from the team-week rows already inside `combined` rather than from a frozen side file. Additionally, strengthen the check at predict.py:350 from "column exists" to "column is not entirely NaN on the live rows when it was mostly populated in training" — that single assertion would have caught this and the routes bug above.

title: 2025+ depth charts pin every post-season and offseason snapshot to week 18, so depth_rank/is_starter for week 18 come from a March snapshot
failure: `_attach_week_from_timestamp` clips any snapshot taken at or after week 18's first kickoff to week 18 (`idx.clip(0, len(week_start)-1)`), and `depth_chart_normalized` then keeps the LATEST snapshot per (team, week, gsis_id) via `drop_duplicates(..., keep="last")` at fetch.py:752. For the 2025 file that latest snapshot is dated 2026-03-14 — after the Super Bowl and after the 2026 league year opened. So `depth_rank`, `depth_rank_capped` and `is_starter`, all classified PREGAME in gridlib/columns.py:106 and all shipped features (USE_DEPTH_RANK = True), carry post-season information for every week-18 row of the 2025 season. Verified: of the 387 week-18 2025 rows in the backfill, 146 of the 382 joinable ones (38.2%) have a depth rank that differs from the last rank published before week 18's kickoff; depth_rank_capped differs on 76 rows and is_starter flips on 36. Kirk Cousins is rank 1 in the pre-kickoff chart (he started, 32 attempts) and rank 2 in the shipped one. The same clipping corrupts scripts/build_availability.py, which fits the served p_play grid on the 2025 charts: week 18 normalizes to 887 (team, player) pairs against ~655 for weeks 16-17, and 212 of those 887 (23.9%) are players who appear on NO snapshot before week 18 kicked off — 2026 offseason additions. title: DataFrame.assign inside the 18-iteration stat loop deep-copies the whole growing feature frame each time
failure: add_player_history loops over the 18 VOLUME_STATS. On each iteration it calls `out.assign(_k=...)` purely to attach a temporary grouping key. Under the pinned pandas 2.3.3 with copy-on-write OFF (verified: `pd.options.mode.copy_on_write` is False, and requirements.txt pins pandas==2.3.3 deliberately), `DataFrame.assign` calls `self.copy(deep=None)`, which for a non-CoW BlockManager resolves to deep=True — a full data copy. The frame being copied grows from 183 to 251 columns across the loop, so each copy is 130-180 MB. Measured directly on a 63,042 x 251 frame: one `assign` call added 154 MB of RSS and `np.shares_memory` between parent and result was False. A/B over the whole loop: with the assign it costs 4.60 s and 879 MB peak; replacing it with a precomputed key Series and a direct groupby costs 1.30 s and 541 MB peak. Isolating just this change (rolling left as shipped) gives 927 MB peak vs 525 MB — the assign alone is ~400 MB of the cold-request peak.
fix:
Build the (gsis_id, season) key once before the loop and use it directly, with no frame copy:
    key = out["gsis_id"].astype(str) + "_" + out["season"].astype(str)   # once, above the loop
    ...
    v = out[col].astype(float).fillna(0.0)
    s_sum = v.groupby(key, sort=False).cumsum() - v
    s_n   = out.groupby(key, sort=False).cumcount().astype(float)
Verified to produce identical values.

title: _prior_roll_mean uses groupby().apply() per player group, 36 times over ~4,700 groups
failure: _prior_roll_mean calls `groupby(...).apply(lambda s: s.shift(1).rolling(window, min_periods=1).mean())`, which runs the lambda once per gsis_id group — roughly 4,700 Python-level calls, each constructing an intermediate Series, then reassembling with a concat and an index reset. add_player_history calls it 36 times (18 VOLUME_STATS x ROLL_WINDOWS of (3, 8)), so ~170,000 per-group Python invocations per feature build. Measured: this accounts for 3.89 s of the 4.60 s add_player_history spends (isolated A/B: apply ON with the assign removed = 3.89 s, apply replaced with the vectorised equivalent = 1.30 s), i.e. roughly 3x the runtime of the function that dominates the 22 s cold request.
fix:
Do the shift and the roll as two grouped ops with no Python callback:
    v = df[col].astype(float).fillna(0.0)
    g = df[key]
    return (v.groupby(g, sort=False).shift(1)
             .groupby(g, sort=False).rolling(window, min_periods=1).mean()
             .reset_index(level=0, drop=True))
Verified equal to the current output (including the NaN pattern).

title: Baseline-served TD targets are zero-filled per row instead of falling back, so mid-season they serve 0.00 and drop the anytime-TD props
failure: receiving_tds and rushing_tds FAIL the gate and are served from the season-to-date mean f_std_{target}. The fallback to f_career_{target} is all-or-nothing: it fires only when base.isna().all(). In week 1 every f_std_* is NaN so the fallback fires and the numbers look right, which is why the live 2026 week-1 board is fine. From week 2 onward f_std_* is populated for most rows, isna().all() is False, and every player who has not yet recorded a stat line this season falls through to .fillna(0.0) and is served 0.00 TDs. That is not the baseline the ship gate measured: validate_models.py:162 fills a NaN baseline-2 with the training-set target mean, not with zero. Downstream, props.py:895 does `if lam <= 0: continue` on lam = rushing_tds + receiving_tds, so those players' anytime-TD prop lines are silently dropped from the compare table (they are counted as neither refused nor unmatched), and predict.fantasy_score understates them by 6.0 points per expected TD, the largest per-unit weight in the whole formula.
fix: Make the fallback per row rather than frame-wide: base = live[f'f_std_{target}'].where(notna, live[f'f_career_{target}']) and only then fill what is still missing, and fill it with the same league constant validate_models.py uses (the training-set mean for those positions) rather than 0.0, so the served baseline is the baseline the gate scored.

title: Baseline target fallback is gated on the whole column being NaN, so mid-season debutants are forced to exactly 0.0 instead of their career rate
failure: For the two baseline-served targets (rushing_tds, receiving_tds), the declared per-player fallback to f_career_{target} only fires when the ENTIRE f_std_{target} column is NaN, i.e. only in week 1. From week 2 onward any player who has not yet played this season has f_std NaN while the column as a whole is populated, so `base` stays f_std and `.fillna(0.0)` writes a hard 0.0 for him. His career rate is discarded. Downstream, gridlib/props.py:895 does `if lam <= 0: continue`, so his anytime-TD prop is deleted from the board entirely, and {target}_expected is 0 for the coherence gates.
fix: Make the fallback per-row, not per-column: `base = live[col].where(live[col].notna(), live.get(fallback))`, and keep NaN (not 0.0) where neither exists so "no history" stays distinguishable from "history of zero".

title: project_week_cached has no in-process memoization or single-flight, so concurrent sessions each run the 1.4 GB build
failure: project_week_cached is disk-cached only. It is called from app.py:185, pages/Game.py, props_ui._freeze_week (line 95) and props_ui.render_week_record (line 589), and none of those call sites is wrapped in @st.cache_data — the only four @st.cache_data decorators in the whole app are on _schedule, _depth and _injuries. Streamlit runs each browser session's script in its own thread inside one process, and there is no lock around the build: two visitors arriving within the same 22-second window on a week with no cached parquet both see `dc_fresh(path)` False and both enter project_week, so the process holds two ~1.4 GB working sets at once. On a ~1 GB container that is a guaranteed OOM kill rather than a slow page. Even in the single-user case there is no memoization: with ttl=3600, the build re-runs every hour, and every widget interaction in between (week arrow, season selectbox, theme toggle, opening the Update lines popover) re-reads the parquet and re-runs the whole props path.
fix: Wrap the call in a module-level `@st.cache_data(ttl=..., show_spinner=...)` helper in app.py / Game.py (Streamlit serializes concurrent misses on the same key, which gives the single-flight for free), or add an explicit threading.Lock keyed on (season, week) around the build inside project_week_cached.

title: grade() silently drops every probability prop, so 321 of 1022 frozen rows can never enter the record

title: GRIDIRONVALUE_READONLY does not stop writes: any anonymous visitor can overwrite or delete the shared committed boards

title: A 15-character paste crashes the whole page and prints server file paths
failure: `parse_prizepicks_json` assumes `data[]` and `included[]` hold dicts. Pasting `{"data": ["x"]}` makes line 231 call `.get` on a str; pasting `{"included": {"a": 1}}` does the same at line 220. `parse_any` catches only `(json.JSONDecodeError, TypeError, ValueError)` at props.py:349, so AttributeError escapes. `resolve_and_persist` is called at app.py:102 and pages/Game.py:112 BEFORE any UI renders, so the exception replaces the entire page. title: passing_tds, passing_interceptions and fg_made are compared as a MEAN against a half-point line, the exact estimand error the file documents for anytime TDs
failure: props.py:129-141 explains that a 0.5 TD line asks P(X>=1) and that E[X] sits above it for every player, and routes rush/rec TDs through "__prob__". The same three low-count integer stats are left on the mean-vs-line rule: "pass tds" (line 98), "interceptions thrown"/"int" (lines 103-104) and "fg made"/"field goals made" (lines 148-149). None of them has a fitted ratio distribution either - build_prob_calibration.py SPECS covers only attempts, completions, passing_yards, carries, rushing_yards, targets, receptions, receiving_yards - so prob_over returns NaN, the median substitution at props.py:943 never runs, and lean falls back to `diff > 0` at props.py:928. For a 0.5 line no distributional assumption is even needed: for any non-negative integer X, E[X] = sum_{k>=1} P(X>=k) >= P(X>=1), so E[INT] > 0.5 does not imply P(INT>=1) > 0.5. On the committed frozen week-1 board, re-scoring with the module's own poisson_at_least at threshold_for_line(line) puts 9 of 32 Pass TDs rows, 12 of 26 INT rows and 7 of 30 FG Made rows on the wrong side - 28 wrong-sided rows out of 88. Examples: Patrick Mahomes INT model 0.62 vs 0.5 -> "More", but P(INT>=1) = 0.462 -> Less. Brock Purdy Pass TDs model 1.53 vs 1.5 -> "More", but P(>=2) = 0.452 -> Less. Over-dispersion, which the file notes at props.py:797, pushes P(>=k) further down and so adds flips rather than removing them.
fix: Route these three through the same "__prob__" path already used for rush/rec TDs: P(X >= threshold_for_line(line)) vs 0.5. They are Poisson-loss models (train_models.py SPECS), so poisson_at_least is the consistent choice.

title: Availability grid counts bye-week depth-chart rows as "did not appear", deflating every p_play cell by about 6%

title: Depth-chart snapshots are bucketed by the week's FIRST kickoff, so every chart published after Thursday night is attributed to the following week and discarded

title: load_release treats a successful but empty fetch as good data, overwriting the cache and returning empty in violation of the module's stale-beats-empty doctrine

For the whole-history files that reuse one filename forever -- games.parquet, players.parquet, officials.parquet, ngs_*.parquet -- that permanently replaces good data with an empty frame until an unrelated good fetch happens to land. load_schedules() likewise only checks `df is None` (line 158), so it returns the empty frame instead of raising, and week_games() then renders "no games this week" on a live board. fix: Add an all-NaN (or near-all-NaN) check on the live slice for every registry feature column, not just a name-presence check: any trained column whose live rows are 100% NaN while the training table had it populated is the same silent-drop failure and should raise with the column name.

title: "Anytime TD" is refused even though STAT_MAP has a working probability mapping for it

title: 77 of 1325 lines are dropped with no counter, so an empty board cannot explain itself

title: apply_level's left clamp INFLATES the smallest projections, the opposite of the bias it exists to correct

title: Calibration parquet carries a 199-element attrs list that pandas deep-copies on every derived object inside _row_for

title: The "Not priced" notice gives one blanket reason ("maxima over plays") for refusals that were refused for entirely different reasons, and REFUSE silently shadows a working mapping for "anytime td"
failure: props.py:872-875 buckets refusals by stat_type -> COUNT and throws away REFUSE's per-stat reason string. props_ui.py:283-290 then lists the refused stat names and appends one fixed sentence: "Longest-anything props are maxima over plays, and a mean-projection model cannot price a maximum." title: is_starter conflates "no depth-chart row" with "not a starter", asserting 0.0 for 3,980 rows including 146 QB starts
failure: depth_rank_capped correctly stays NaN when the depth-chart merge misses, but is_starter is derived as (depth_rank_capped == 1).astype(float), and NaN == 1 evaluates False, so every unmatched row is stamped 0.0 -- an affirmative claim that the player was not a starter, indistinguishable from a genuine backup. 3,980 of 63,042 player-games (6.3%) have a null depth_rank; 146 of them are quarterbacks who threw 20 or more passes, i.e. unambiguous starters. is_starter is in models/registry_m1.json feature_columns, so a tree learns those 146 QB starts as backup rows. This is the same shape as the missingness leak the project already fixed for the red-zone counts (build_player_week.py:237-244), applied in the opposite direction.
fix: df["is_starter"] = df["depth_rank_capped"].eq(1).astype(float).where(df["depth_rank_capped"].notna()) so the unknown case stays NaN and a tree routes it as missing rather than as a confident "not a starter". Mirror the change in gridlib/predict.py:210, which has the identical expression.

title: build_weather marks a venue-season complete after any single fetched game, so in-season venues never get weather for their later games
failure: The resume set is keyed on (stadium_id, season) and is populated from any previously written row for that venue-season, while the archive request is capped at `cutoff` = yesterday (line 134, 143). There is also no forecast path at all: FORECAST is defined at line 53 and never referenced, so an unplayed game can never receive weather, contradicting the claim in gridlib/columns.py:126-129 that serving values are forecast weather.
fix: Key done_pairs on game_id, not (stadium_id, season), so only games that actually got a row are skipped; and route games whose kickoff is beyond the archive cutoff to the FORECAST endpoint that is already declared.

title: test_shrink_cannot_cross_a_coin_flip re-implements the shrink inside the test; production prob_over is never called
failure: The body computes `shrunk = 0.5 + (raw - 0.5) * (1.0 - U.SHRINK)` itself and asserts the sign is preserved. If the applied form were changed (a different centre, or applied before the interp instead of after) the test would still pass. The companion test_shrink_is_actually_applied (line 985) does call prob_over, but only checks an upper bound, so it cannot see a sign flip near 0.5 either.

title: Scheduled weekly refresh will be auto-disabled over the offseason before it ever reaches week 1
failure: The only trigger for the refresh is `cron: "0 13 * * 2"` on a public repository. GitHub disables scheduled workflows in public repos after 60 days with no repository activity, and this job's own steps produce no commit in the offseason: from the last February commit through late August every Tuesday run takes the `no change this week` branch (weekly.yml:103), so nothing pushes and the 60-day clock is never reset by the job itself. The workflow is then disabled and the first in-season Tuesday silently does not run — no failure notification, no commit — and the site serves the frozen 2016-2025 history all season (the exact staleness described in weekly.yml's own header). `workflow_dispatch` exists but requires someone to remember.
fix: Either keep the repo active over the offseason (the committed weekly board pastes already do this in season, but not Feb-Aug), or add a cheap keepalive step, or accept it and add a preseason checklist item to re-enable the workflow in the Actions tab.

title: Positional-defence league prior falls back to a full-panel mean that includes the current and future seasons
failure: `add_positional_defense` builds its league prior correctly as an expanding mean over STRICTLY prior seasons (features.py:706-709), then fills the resulting NaN with `allowed.groupby("position")[s].transform("mean")` — the mean over every row in the frame, including the row's own season, every later season, and (at serve time) the zero-valued rows constructed for the upcoming game. Measured on the shipped backfill this fires on 2,701 of 27,538 defence-game-position rows (9.8%), all of them season 2016, and it feeds the empirical-Bayes prior for f_dvp_targets / f_dvp_receiving_yards / f_dvp_carries / f_dvp_rushing_yards on every 2016 row. The contaminating quantity is a per-position constant (WR 19.345, TE 7.070, RB 6.168 targets allowed per defence-game), so it cannot leak any single row's outcome, but it does embed 2017-2025 league levels into 2016 features and it violates the module's own stated rule. It is the same shape as the two leaks the file documents, just smaller.
fix: Fall back to a within-season-so-far prior computed with the same cumsum-minus-current discipline used everywhere else in the module, or leave the first season's f_dvp_* as NaN and let the tree route it — either is point-in-time honest. Cheapest correct option: restrict the fallback mean to `allowed[allowed["season"] < row season]` and accept NaN when there is nothing earlier.

title: Depth-chart FB label vs backfill RB label: the same player trains as a receiver and is served with FB-scale defence-vs-position

title: fantasy_score returns 0.0 for a row with no projected components, and compare()'s fantasy branch is the only one with no NaN guard
failure: fantasy_score starts at 0.0 and skips every NaN component, so a row where every PP_SCORING column is NaN returns exactly 0.0 - indistinguishable from a genuine zero projection. If a model artifact is deleted or fails to deploy, the target becomes NaN while its _source column still reads "model", and the only signal is a logger.warning at default level WARNING going to stderr. Mean props for that stat are then silently dropped by props.compare (adding to the 77 uncounted lines), and every affected player's Fantasy Score silently loses that stat's entire contribution - e.g. deleting passing_yards_m1.joblib drops every QB fantasy composite by roughly 10 points with the row still badged "composed" and no "baseline" or "low conf" marker in the ledger.
fix: Move the artifact check ahead of the source stamp and set the source to something like "unavailable", or raise - a missing artifact for a shipped target is a deployment error, not a degradation to absorb.

title: p_play falls back to a hardcoded 0.5 for any (position, rank) cell the availability grid does not contain

title: parse_prizepicks_json raises an uncaught AttributeError when data[] or included[] holds a non-dict
failure: The loops call p.get("type") (line 231) and inc.get("type") (line 220) without checking that the element is a mapping. A payload that is valid JSON but whose data[] or included[] contains a string or number raises AttributeError: 'str' object has no attribute 'get'. parse_any's handler at line 349 catches only (json.JSONDecodeError, TypeError, ValueError), so AttributeError escapes parse_any, escapes resolve_and_persist, and reaches Streamlit as a red traceback on app.py:102 - before any page content renders. Everything else in this parser is defensive about shape (isinstance checks on raw, `or {}` on attributes/relationships, _person_like on names), so this is the one hole.
fix: Add `if not isinstance(p, dict): continue` / `if not isinstance(inc, dict): continue` at the top of both loops, and add AttributeError to parse_any's except tuple as a backstop.

title: Touchdown probabilities bypass the FLOOR/CEIL rule and render as "0%" on the board
failure: uncertainty.py:31-34 states "Never return certainty. A model that says 0% is claiming an outcome is impossible" and clamps prob_over to [0.01, 0.99]. poisson_at_least has no such clamp - it clamps only to [0.0, 1.0] at props.py:810 - and its output is what props_ui._fmt_model prints for kind=="probability" as f"{100*model:.0f}%". The board therefore prints the impossibility claim the sibling module exists to forbid.
fix: Apply the same FLOOR/CEIL clamp to poisson_at_least's return value, or clamp in compare() where model_val is set for the probability branch.

title: route_to_weeks rescans and re-tz-converts the whole season schedule once per pasted line
failure: For every row of a pasted board, route_to_weeks recomputes `(reg["kickoff"].dt.tz_convert("UTC") - ts).abs()` over the full regular-season games frame (272 rows) and then calls `.mode()` on the match. That is O(lines x games): 1,325 x 272 = ~360,000 datetime subtractions plus 1,325 mode() calls per paste. Measured at 0.31 s for the committed 1,325-line board (0.24 ms per line). This runs inside resolve_and_persist, which is called at the top of both app.py and pages/Game.py on every rerun where pp_paste is non-empty.
fix: Convert the kickoff column to UTC once outside the loop, then resolve all lines at once with a merge_asof or a numpy searchsorted against the sorted kickoff array with a 6-hour tolerance.

title: "anytime td" is in both STAT_MAP and REFUSE; REFUSE wins, so the probability-routing comment is false for that key
failure: The comment at lines 122-136 says anytime-touchdown props are "Routed to a PROBABILITY, never to a mean, and this is a correctness fix rather than a preference", and STAT_MAP:137 maps "anytime td" to the __prob__ path. _resolve_stat checks REFUSE first, and REFUSE:164 contains "anytime td", so any board posting that stat_type is refused with "a probability, not a mean; needs a scoring model" and counted under meta["refused"] — the STAT_MAP entry is unreachable. The reason string is also wrong: a scoring model exists (poisson_at_least on rushing_tds + receiving_tds). The 2026 week 1 board happens to label these "Player Touchdowns", which is mapped, so nothing is lost today; a board using the other label silently drops all of them.

title: Fantasy Score rows carry a neutral "unmeasured" badge and rank in the same band as "weak", above every "no edge" row, despite being composed mostly of the two models that failed the ship gate
failure: reliability_for(()) returns tier "unmeasured" for the fantasy composite (verified by call), so _tier_badge renders the label "unmeasured" with the tooltip "Side-picking accuracy not measured for this stat", which reads as neutral. rank_by_reliability maps unknown tiers to TIER_ORDER.get(t, 2) -- the same rank as "weak" -- so Fantasy Score sorts above all 382 "no edge" rows. props_ui.py:329 defines weak_tiers = {"negative", "none"}, so the "N of these are stats where a lean is not evidence" notice never names Fantasy Score. But predict.fantasy_score (predict.py:436-448) documents that the composite "inherits the touchdown problem: two of the three touchdown terms are served from a baseline rather than a model, and they carry the largest per-unit weight in the whole formula" (6.0 points each), and its own docstring says no uncertainty band can be honest for it because the components are correlated. It also gets no median correction and no P(Over): cols == ("__fantasy__",) is excluded at props.py:931, so the lean comes from the mean-minus-line gap, the exact rule the site abandoned for skewed stats. On the live week-1 board this is 130 of 1022 rows -- 13% of the board and the second-largest stat.
fix: Give the fantasy composite its own tier that inherits the worst of its components (so it lands in "no edge" and in the "lean is not evidence" notice), and make TIER_ORDER default place "unmeasured" last rather than mid-table.

title: Injury status interpolated unescaped into a quoted class attribute

This is the single interpolation in store.py that breaks the file's own stated rule at store.py:5-7 ("every interpolated value passes through util.esc first").
fix: Slugify or escape the class fragment, e.g. `re.sub(r'[^a-z0-9-]', '', status.lower())`, or at minimum `esc(status.lower())`.

title: render.yaml ships the app with CORS and XSRF protection both disabled
failure: The committed Render start command passes `--server.enableCORS false` and `--server.enableXsrfProtection false`. With both off, Streamlit accepts websocket and POST traffic from any origin with no XSRF token, so a page on any other site can open a session against the app and drive its widgets. Combined with the unguarded `_clear_lines` (finding 2, which on Render is not even nominally read-only since DEPLOY.md:66 says GRIDIRONVALUE_READONLY is left unset there), a cross-origin page can delete the saved boards. DEPLOY.md:62 states render.yaml "is kept and still correct", so this is a live configuration, not dead text.
fix: Drop `--server.enableXsrfProtection false`. Render's proxy does not require it; only enableCORS false is needed behind their proxy, and Streamlit supports XSRF protection with CORS off.
